<section begin=par104 />{{GHGpar-heading|104|Conjunctions}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|104|a}}
'''1.''' The conjunctions serve to connect sentences, and to express their relations one to another. They may be either—

(''a'') Original pronouns, e.g. the demonstrative {{GHGheb|text=כִּי|translate=that, because, for}}.

(''b'') Original substantives, which afterwards were reduced to the rank of pronouns, adverbs, or conjunctions; so perhaps {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} (see § 36), which is sometimes used to express the general idea of relation, sometimes as a relative pronoun (properly a demonstrative), but in many cases stands simply for {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}}; also {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} (''nothing''), ''that not''; {{GHGheb|text=פֶּן־|translate=that not}} (the Greek μή of ''prohibition''), &c. To these may be added the adverbial combination of substantives with prepositions, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּטֶ֫רֶם}}<section end=par104 /><noinclude>
